messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High 5xx rate and continuous_batch_size growth detected on prod-serving. Affected model: llama-2-13b-q4. KV cache evictions spike. P95 latency climbing.

maria: saw the pager. I'm on it — pulling logs and dashboard now.

aj: oncall here. can you paste the alert graph?

maria: pasting short stack:
```
alerts: kv_cache_evictions_per_min > 1000 for 3m
metric: continuous_batch_avg_size jumped 24 -> 180 over 2m
model: llama-2-13b-q4 (migratory variant)
error: out_of_memory / kernel-timeouts on several workers
```

devon: who deployed last night? any batch config changes?

kevin: deployment history shows a config tweak at 02:12 UTC — increased max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 8192 for llama-2-13b-q4. "auto_prefetch": true also flipped.

maria: that matches timeline. suspect prefetch + larger batch token caps causing KV cache pressure on prefix-heavy traffic (cold-starts). Customers with longer context (few enterprise customers) hit hot path.

aj: initial mitigation ideas: 1) throttle prefetch on llama-2-13b-q4 2) temporarily cap continuous_batch_size 3) fallback to smaller model variant (llama-2-7b-q4) for tiered customers. thoughts?

devon: agree. let's be surgical: flip auto_prefetch=false for the model pool, set max_batch_tokens back to 4096, and put a soft rate limit on cold-starts (50 rps per node).

maria: I'm executing a config rollback to the model pool now (will update runbook).

runbook-bot: ACTION_LOCK acquires: rollback-config on pool llama-2-13b-q4. Confirm with @maria to proceed.

maria: confirmed. rolling back. monitoring for eviction rate.

[~2112346200] maria: rollback applied. now setting continuous_batch_size cap to 64 (was unbounded).

kevin: adding temporary routing rule to divert requests above 30s latency to llama-2-7b-q4 with cached prefix support.

cs-team-bot: Notifying Customer Success: customers with long context windows may see degraded quality while we fallback models. Sending advisory to top 3 customers.

aj: monitoring dashboards... eviction rate down 60% in last 3m. p95 latency dropping but still elevated for a subset.

maria: logs show repeated prefix-KV replication attempts that were inflating cache footprint. Looks like cold-start churn + aggressive prefetch caused lots of unique prefixes to populate KV.

devon: run controlled restart on 4 of 12 workers in the pool to flush bad KV shards. Doing rolling restarts with 30s pause.

maria: restart done on first 4. errors on those nodes decreased. overall cluster memory usage dropping.

aj: customers: one high-volume partner saw 15% 5xx spike for ~8 minutes. CS notified. No SLA breach expected but we should log incident.

kevin: adding a short-term admission control rule: any request with > 4 prefix variants will be queued and sampled (to reduce prefix explosion).

maria: agreed. patching admission control now.

[~2112348200] aj: eviction rate near normal. continuous_batch_avg_size back to ~30. p95 latency within SLO for 95% traffic. small tail remains for enterprise long-context cases on a few shards.

devon: next steps: 1) author hotfix to make auto_prefetch opt-in per-route (not global) 2) add metrics for unique_prefix_rate per model 3) run a replay test with enterprise traces to validate admission controls.

maria: I'll open a follow-up RFC for prefetch opt-in and change control. Also will schedule a post-incident evaluation with SRE, Runtime, and Product to decide default prefetch behavior.

aj: tagging this as P2 with customer impact documented. Please fill out incident template and timeline.

cs-team-bot: CS notified customers A,B,C with advisory: temporary fallback to 7b model for long contexts; suggested mitigation: shorten context or batch fewer distinct prefixes.

maria: filing timeline in ops-incident board. initial root cause: combined config change (max_batch_tokens + auto_prefetch) + high unique-prefix cold-start workload => KV cache blowup and eviction storm.

devon: long-term mitigation ideas mentioned in-thread + automated canary for prefetch flips to detect cache growth within 5 minutes.

maria: thanks all — I'll do the handoff to next oncall in 30m and include the rollback and restart steps in the handoff note.

aj: handing to kevin for overnight watch. kevin you'll have the runbook entry in incident ticket #INC-211234.

kevin: got it. I'll keep watch and run extra sampling of enterprise shards. If eviction rate > 200/min open pager immediately.

maria: closing slack loop — will post postmortem draft in #postmortems tomorrow. Good job. :thumbsup:

runbook-bot: INCIDENT_NOTE: rollback applied, continuous_batch cap=64, auto_prefetch=false, 4/12 workers restarted, routing fallback enabled to llama-2-7b-q4. Pager threshold set: eviction_rate > 200/min.

cs-team-bot: Incident advisory logged and CS ticket created (#CS-7721).

kevin: leaving a short summary for next oncall:
- what happened: cold-start+prefetch + larger batch cap => KV prefix explosion -> eviction storm -> latency/5xx
- immediate actions: rollback config, cap continuous_batch_size, rolling restarts, route heavy tails to 7b
- followups: opt-in prefetch RFC, unique_prefix_rate metric, canary for prefetch flips

maria: last check — metrics stable. handing off.

kevin: acknowledged. oncall handoff complete.
